{{Short description|Dutch mathematician (1904–1964)}}
[[File:Jurjen Koksma, 1930.jpg|thumb|Jurjen Koksma, 1930]]
[[File:Koksma Titelblatt.jpg|thumb|''Diophantische Approximationen'' (1936), title page.]] 
'''Jurjen Ferdinand Koksma''' (21 April 1904, [[Heerenveen|Schoterland]] &ndash; 17 December 1964, [[Amsterdam]]) was a Dutch [[mathematician]] who specialized in [[analytic number theory]].<ref>[http://bwnw.cwi-incubator.nl/cgi-bin/uncgi/toon?nr=34&ftnr=1 Jurjen Ferdinand Koksma] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071010104113/http://bwnw.cwi-incubator.nl/cgi-bin/uncgi/toon?nr=34&ftnr=1 |date=2007-10-10 }} at the [http://www.bwnw.nl/index.html Biographical Dictionary of Dutch Mathematicians] {{Webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080416044826/http://www.bwnw.nl/index.html |date=2008-04-16 }}</ref>

Koksma received his [[Ph.D.]] degree (''[[cum laude]]'') in 1930 at the [[University of Groningen]] under supervision of [[Johannes van der Corput]], with a thesis on ''Systems of Diophantine Inequalities''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=49633}}</ref> Around the same time, aged 26, he was invited to become full professor at the ''[[Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam]]''. He accepted and in 1930 became the first professor in mathematics at this university.<ref>See van Deursen.</ref> Koksma is also one of the founders of the Dutch ''Mathematisch Centrum'' (today ''[[Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica]]'').

One of Koksma's main works was the book ''Diophantische Approximationen'', published in 1936 by Springer. He also wrote several papers with [[Paul Erdős]].

In 1950 he became member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |author= |url=http://www.dwc.knaw.nl/biografie/pmknaw/?pagetype=authorDetail&aId=PE00001328 |title=Jurjen Ferdinand Koksma (1904 - 1964) |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |access-date=28 July 2015}}</ref>

Koksma had two brothers, Jan and Marten, who were also mathematicians.
